print.notes: Print original is a photographic reproduction of a real book's cover/title/copyright/contents page (references/_gemini/gold-2-A/page-077.png), not encoded as running text anywhere in the source .txt. Neither independent transcription run modelled it into print.blocks (both left print.blocks empty); this reconciliation viewed the page image directly to confirm the braille.lines transcription and the sample's own title/rule citation, but likewise leaves print.blocks empty -- building a faithful print.blocks model of a photographed book cover is out of this reconciliation's scope (reconciling two existing transcription runs), not a disagreement between them to resolve.

resolution: braille.lines: A and B agree byte-for-byte. illustrates.quote: A's rule text was verbatim-correct but scoped to the whole lettered rule (plus, in some files, a stray page-footer line glued in by the extraction) rather than the specific numbered sub-item/cross-reference this example cites; B's own quote field was not a quote at all (it echoed the file's own title/caption). Re-derived directly from source-lines-1390-2934.txt, scoped to exactly the cited rule id.
